# Bidirectional (V2G) chargers for commercial fleet depots in Germany, 2026

## Summary
Depot-scale bidirectional charging in Germany moved from pilots to procurement in 2026, driven by the EnWG Section 14a grid-fee reductions for controllable loads. Three vendors account for roughly two thirds of installed depot units.

## Vendors

| Vendor | HQ | Share of installed depot V2G units (DE) | Typical price, 22 kW AC bidirectional unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| VoltHaven | Hamburg | 31% | EUR 6,900 |
| Ladewerk Systems | Stuttgart | 21% | EUR 7,450 |
| GridNest | Munich | 14% | EUR 6,200 (requires GridNest energy-management subscription) |

## Key findings
- VoltHaven is the market leader, supplying the two largest parcel-delivery fleets.
- Average payback for depots participating in frequency-containment markets is 4.5 years.
- DC bidirectional units (50 kW+) remain rare outside bus depots and cost EUR 28,000-35,000.

## Sources
[1] VoltHaven fleet products: https://www.volthaven.de/en/fleet
[2] Ladewerk Systems pricing sheet 2026: https://ladewerk.de/downloads/preise-2026.pdf
[3] BNetzA Section 14a guidance: https://www.bundesnetzagentur.de/14a

# Bidirectional home chargers

Residential V2H/V2G wallboxes in Europe cost EUR 3,500-5,000. The best-selling unit in 2026 is the HomeLoop Duo at EUR 3,990.
